134	### Known gaps
135	- Retained approvals backed by a delegated run: `ReviewRunStillGoverns` requires the run's bundle to equal what the scope prepares today, so a done spec whose inputs drifted after sealing, whatever the cause, cannot retain a run-backed approval. This spec removes the cause that every sole-member spec hit at the transition to done; routine drift later is left to the follow-up below.
136	- The no-checkpoint stop is covered at the decision (`closeoutStopLeavesNoCheckpoint`) and at the helper both entry paths share, which clears an older checkpoint and names where the state is (`stopOnUnstableInputs`, the path of a call made after the stop and the path inside the apply loop); an end-to-end apply that produces an unknown read view is not covered, because no fixture of this repository can provoke one without a Git failure mid-apply (a Git that cannot be read at all fails the plan instead).
137	- Measured: 17 done specs of this repository gain the criterion; `review verify` gives the same answer for each with the engine before and after (closed, fresh, approved).
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 7. Final Report
142	
143	### Delivered scope
144	A done spec that is the only member of a milestone with a declared exit gate keeps the gate criterion in its review plan when the governing sealed bundle carries it, so the bundle it was sealed with still represents its inputs and the attested approval stays fresh across the transition to done (R1). A done spec sealed without the criterion, a spec of several members, a milestone without a gate and a spec of a terminal roadmap are prepared as before (R2); an open spec still owes the criterion (R3). `pose close --apply` and `--resume` write no checkpoint, and clear the one they hold, when the terminal verification of a done scope stops on an unknown governance read view (R4); every other stop records as before (R5). The attestation rules did not change (R6). Left out: retaining run-backed approvals over later drift, and any change to how a reviewer judges the gate.
145	
146	### Files and modules changed
147	- pose-mcp/internal/pose (review_plan.go, closeout_plan.go, done_spec_sealed_plan_test.go)
148	- pose-mcp/internal/cli (closeout_plan.go, closeout_unstable_inputs_test.go)
149	- ADR a-milestone-of-one-member-is-that-member (amendment); the validation matrix gains `done-spec-keeps-its-sealed-plan-integration`
150	
151	### Validation executed
152	- Command: `pose validate --strict --jobs 4` on a clean clone of the reviewed head, and the suites of `internal/pose`, `internal/cli` and `internal/mcpserver`
153	- Result: recorded by the sealed validation evidence; independent delegated review by a different vendor, concluded with `pose review conclude`.
154	
155	### Residual risks
156	- The criterion is kept by the criterion id found in the governing bundle's plan: a bundle sealed with a gate that the roadmap later changed keeps a plan whose description is the current one, not the sealed one, and reads as drifted, which is what it would have done before.
157	- The checkpoint rule is keyed on the plan's read view not being current; a plan that reports another reason for a blocked verify still records.
158	
159	### Follow-ups
160	
161	- [open] Let a done spec retain an approval backed by a delegated run over routine drift after sealing: `ReviewRunStillGoverns` compares the run's bundle with what the scope prepares today, which a completed scope never matches once anything moved.
